How many subnets and hosts per subnet does 172.16.0.0/19 give?
A - 3 bits borrowed = 8 subnets (subnet-zero allowed); 13 host bits = 8,190 hosts. If subnet-zero were disallowed you would count 6 or 7.
What is the broadcast address of 172.30.99.255/22?
172.30.99.255 - /22  block 4 in the third octet: 96, 100  the subnet is 172.30.96.0 and the broadcast is 99.255, so this host address IS the broadcast and is not a valid host.

Check: 128 + 64 + 32 + 4 + 4 = 232 addresses used. Space left: 192.168.50.232 - .255 (24 addresses) for growth. No overlaps. Why largest first? A big block must start on a boundary that is a multiple of its size, so placing it last can leave gaps you cannot fill.

16 subnets, 4,094 hosts - 4 bits borrowed; 12 host bits.
Why does the broadcast address of the last subnet always end with 255 (for a Class C)?
The last subnet's host bits are all 1s, and in a Class C the subnet ends at the last address of the network - e.g. 192.168.10.255.
